title: United States announces cluster munitions in a new military aid package for Ukraine
body:
On 7 July 2023 the US Department of Defense announced a new security assistance package for Ukraine worth up to 800 million US dollars. It included Patriot and HIMARS munitions and additional artillery systems and ammunition. For the first time, the United States also agreed to provide cluster munitions to Ukraine. These were dual-purpose improved conventional munitions (DPICM), 155 mm artillery rounds that disperse submunitions, drawn from Department of Defense stocks.

The Pentagon said the rounds had a dud rate of 2.35 percent and contrasted this with Russian cluster munitions, for which it said dud rates were as high as 40 percent. Colin Kahl, the US Under Secretary of Defense for Policy, cited the urgency of the moment and said hundreds of thousands of artillery rounds could be provided immediately. He said Ukraine had given written assurances that it would not use the munitions in populated urban areas and would carefully account for their use. The Department of Defense said Ukraine had also committed to mine-clearing efforts after the conflict to reduce civilian impact.

In a CNN interview, President Joe Biden called it a difficult decision and said he had discussed it with allies and congressional contacts. He said that the Ukrainians were running out of ammunition. The package was the 42nd drawdown from Department of Defense inventories for Ukraine since August 2021, and the Biden administration had committed more than 41.3 billion dollars in security assistance since February 2022.
